verses.text: Observe the month of Abib, and keep the Passover to Yahweh your God; for in the month of Abib Yahweh your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
You shall sacrifice the Passover to Yahweh your God, of the flock and the herd, in the place which Yahweh shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there.

You shall eat no leavened bread with it. You shall eat unleavened bread with it seven days, even the bread of affliction; for you came out of the land of Egypt in haste; that you may remember the day when you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
No yeast shall be seen with you in all your borders seven days; neither shall any of the meat, which you sacrifice the first day at evening, remain all night until the morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover within any of your gates, which Yahweh your God gives you;

but at the place which Yahweh your God shall choose, to cause his name to dwell in, there you shall sacrifice the Passover at evening, at the going down of the sun, at the season that you came out of Egypt.
You shall roast and eat it in the place which Yahweh your God chooses. In the morning you shall return to your tents.
Six days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly to Yahweh your God. You shall do no work.
You shall count for yourselves seven weeks. From the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
You shall keep the feast of weeks to Yahweh your God with a tribute of a freewill offering of your hand, which you shall give, according as Yahweh your God blesses you.

You shall rejoice before Yahweh your God: you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite who is within your gates, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, who are among you, in the place which Yahweh your God shall choose to cause his name to dwell there.
You shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt. You shall observe and do these statutes.
You shall keep the feast of tents seven days, after you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your wine press.
You shall rejoice in your feast, you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, who are within your gates.

You shall keep a feast to Yahweh your God seven days in the place which Yahweh chooses; because Yahweh your God will bless you in all your increase, and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful.

Three times in a year all of your males shall appear before Yahweh your God in the place which he chooses: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tents. They shall not appear before Yahweh empty.
Every man shall give as he is able, according to Yahweh your God’s blessing which he has given you.
You shall make judges and officers in all your gates, which Yahweh your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
You shall not pervert justice. You shall not show partiality. You shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous.
You shall follow that which is altogether just, that you may live, and inherit the land which Yahweh your God gives you.
You shall not plant for yourselves an Asherah of any kind of tree beside Yahweh your God’s altar, which you shall make for yourselves.
Neither shall you set yourself up a sacred stone which Yahweh your God hates.

footnotes.content: The month of remembrance. Abib means the green ear—spring, new life, when God broke Egypt's chains and brought His people into freedom. Each year, mark it: look back at deliverance and forward to the God who keeps His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The place He will choose—not many altars, but one. Even in the wilderness, God called them to worship where His name dwells. Bring the best of your flock and herd: He asks what matters most to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Unleavened bread, the bread of affliction. No time for the yeast to rise—they fled in haste. But why remember haste, year after year? So they never forget the Lord ran ahead of them in their darkest hour and brought them safely out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No yeast in sight for seven days. The old pattern had to go; the new way required a clean break. Sometimes the Lord calls us to put away what once sustained us so we learn to depend only on Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not in your gates—not at home, not alone. Worship at God's appointed place pulls the people together, rich and poor, old and young. The Lord wanted them in one place, remembering one deliverance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At sunset, at the hour they came out of Egypt. The timing itself was a lesson: the Lord's work is often done when day fails and darkness seems about to win. Yet redemption comes at twilight, and morning follows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Roast and eat it, then return to your tents in the morning. The feast was brief—one night to remember forever. Some of the Lord's deepest work happens in a single night, and then we live the rest of our lives grateful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six days of unleavened bread. The seventh day—solemn rest, no work. The pattern was clear: work and remember together, but one day for God alone. Rest isn't laziness; it's trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Count seven weeks from the sickle to the standing grain—fifty days. Counting itself is worship, each day a step toward remembering. We mark time by noticing what God has done, not just by living through it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bring a freewill offering, measured by what He blessed you with. Not a burden, but joy—giving back because He gave first. The measure of our gratitude is the measure of His faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rejoice with your son, daughter, servants, the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, the widow. Joy was never meant to be private. The feast gathers all the people, especially the ones the world forgets. That's the heart of God right there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Remember you were a slave in Egypt. Gratitude is the twin of obedience—when we truly remember what He saved us from, we keep His statutes not from fear but from love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The feast of tents comes after harvest, when the work is done and the barns are full. Joy doesn't come from worry about tomorrow—it comes when we've laid our burden down and rest in His provision.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again—rejoice with the servant, the foreigner, the fatherless, the widow. The Lord circles back to the same truth: if you're glad, so is the whole household. One man's joy that forgets the poor isn't joy at all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keep the feast seven days because the Lord will bless your increase and the work of your hands. Here's the secret: blessing and obedience aren't separate. When you keep His way, you're already living in His abundance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three times a year, all males appear before Yahweh at the place He chooses. Not empty-handed, not empty-hearted. These gatherings wove the nation together and kept the Lord at the center of every season.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Give as you are able, according to His blessing. There's no fixed amount—the measure is what He gave you. A widow's two coins outweigh a rich man's abundance when the heart is full of gratitude.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Make judges and officers in your gates. The shift is striking: from celebration and provision to justice and truth. A society that feasts together but judges unjustly is rotten at its core.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't pervert justice, show partiality, or take a bribe—it blinds the eyes of the wise. Money can cloud even the clearest mind. When we're tempted to bend the truth, we're always losing more than we gain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Follow altogether just measures so you may live and inherit the land. Justice isn't a burden or a luxury—it's the condition of life. A people that lives by righteousness inherits blessing; those who don't, lose everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No Asherah trees beside Yahweh's altar. The Lord's altar stands alone. We set things up beside Him—custom, comfort, our own way—and call them worship. But He calls it idolatry.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No sacred stones the Lord hates. Readers today hear an echo in this: we still raise up what the Lord despises and call it holy. Yet He remains faithful to those who turn back to Him alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
